key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than trap light: they can also improve wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texture engineering is a multi-functional design strategy that can raise efficiency and reliability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Use nano/micro-textured surfaces to reduce reflection and enhance light trapping.
Tune texture geometry to improve perovskite-solution wetting and film formation.
Leverage texture-induced effects on crystal growth, carrier extraction, and flexible-device durability.
evidence_signal: The abstract summarizes a review of very recently reported texture-related benefits across perovskite solar cells, focusing on outcomes such as grain size, crystal orientation, open-circuit voltage, and bending stability.
watch_item: Reported benefits are review-based and likely texture- and process-dependent, so gains may not transfer directly across materials, fabrication routes, or device stacks.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
